newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst sees considerable savings with Clariant.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst sees considerable savings with Clariant.

text.p: German Hoechst AG, Europe's largest chemicals group, said on Tuesday its plan to merge its speciality chemicals business with Swiss group Clariant AG into a new group would save each partner considerable amounts of money.
"The synergies should be around 600 million marks ($385.5 million) or 500 million Swiss francs for each group," Hoechst board member Karl-Gerhard Seifert told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Seifert said the merger would also result in the loss of around 5,000 jobs over the next three years. Currently the two groups together employ 31,000 in the specialty chemicals area.
Seifert said Hoechst will hold a 40 to 45 percent stake in Clariant and that the group is expected to grow in coming years.

Acknowledging that Hoechst's specialty chemicals business has been an underperformer for some time, Seifert said the new company would have much more growth potential. "The intended plan is for the company to grow in the area of specialty chemicals," Seifert said.

Seifert declined to give the forecast results for Hoechst's specialty chemicals division for 1996, saying only Hoechst would contribute sales of 6.5 billion marks to the new Clarion group, slated to begin operations on July 1, 1997.

Apart from the food ingredients business, which Hoechst will keep, Hoechst "will not have an specialty chemicals anymore after the business is merged. This shows Hoechst is taking one more step to focus on life sciences," Seifert said.
